memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'"If someone brings a lamb as their sin offering, they are to bring a female without defect. They are to lay their hand on its head and slaughter it for a sin offering at the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered."'" - Lev 4:32-33 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
One more option. A goat or a lamb — whichever the household could manage. God is still making room, right to the end of the chapter.

But pause on the picture itself. A person guilty of sin lays a hand on a spotless lamb, and the lamb dies in their place.

That image was performed thousands upon thousands of times across Israel's history. Every generation saw it. Children grew up watching it. And it was preparing a nation for a moment.

When John the Baptist saw Jesus walking toward him, he did not say "here is the Teacher" or "here is the King." He said, "Look, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!" (Jn 1:29). Israel had a thousand years of context for that sentence.

Isaiah had already seen it: He was led like a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before its shearers is silent, so he did not open his mouth (Isa 53:7).

And in Revelation, the centre of heaven's worship is a Lamb, looking as if it had been slain (Rev 5:6). The image never fades. It is not a stage Christianity outgrew. It is the eternal centre of everything.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When I picture Jesus, do I see the Lamb who died in my place?
2. What does it mean that heaven's worship centres on a slain Lamb?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lamb of God, You took away my sin. I lay my hand on You by faith and I worship You. Amen.
